reason: Quantum relative entropy generalizes the classical Kullback–Leibler divergence, not mutual information. The Holevo quantity bounds the accessible information.

fix.summary: QKD security and channel capacities are written in Shannon-type entropies. The Shor–Preskill BB84 key rate uses the binary entropy h(Q), the Holevo quantity χ bounds the accessible classical information, and quantum relative entropy generalizes the Kullback–Leibler divergence.

reason: The cradle showed missing thermalization in a near-integrable gas. GGE relaxation was measured separately (Langen et al. 2015). Slow integrability breaking should be stated.

fix.summary: Bethe-ansatz-integrable systems such as the Lieb–Liniger gas have extensively many conserved charges and relax to a generalized Gibbs ensemble, not a Gibbs state. The quantum Newton's cradle showed near-integrable 1D Bose gases failing to thermalize, and split 1D gases showed GGE relaxation directly. Weak integrability breaking leads to eventual thermalization.

reason: A fractional BBR uncertainty near 1e-20 is overstated; cryogenic and best clocks reach roughly 1e-18 to 1e-19. A T^6 dynamic correction also applies.

fix.summary: The ambient Planck field Stark-shifts clock transitions by a leading amount ∝T⁴, plus a smaller dynamic correction ∝T⁶. It is a leading systematic of optical lattice clocks and has driven cryogenic and well-characterized thermal environments, with BBR uncertainties at the 10⁻¹⁸–10⁻¹⁹ level.

reason: Interactions and finite size shift T_c from the ideal-gas value, so this needs a breaks and is not an identity.

fix.summary: The BEC transition predicted by Bose–Einstein counting, nλ³=ζ(3/2), was realized in 1995 in dilute alkali gases. Harmonic traps change the density of states (k_BT_c≈0.94ħω̄N^{1/3}), and interactions and finite size shift T_c by a few percent, a shift that has been measured.
fix.breaks: Ideal-gas T_c is exact only for non-interacting bosons. Weak interactions shift it and change the critical behaviour to the 3D XY class.

reason: This is a derivation of one from the other, not the same law in both notes. Which particles are bosons comes from the spin–statistics theorem, not the postulate.

fix.summary: Bose and Fermi occupation numbers follow from the symmetrization postulate: states live in the symmetric or antisymmetric N-particle space. Gibbs' 1/N! (the resolution of the mixing paradox) is its classical limit when nλ³≪1. Which species are bosons is fixed by the spin–statistics theorem of relativistic QFT.

reason: Field-level generic overlap that is mislabelled as identity. The specific content is in C1371 (Lindblad/master equation) and C1373/C1374 (quantum fluctuation theorems).
Prosen's solution borrows the DEHP matrix-product technique. It is a method transfer, not an identity, because quantum coherences have no classical counterpart.

fix.summary: Boundary-driven Lindblad XXZ chains are the quantum counterpart of boundary-driven exclusion processes. Prosen solved their steady states with a matrix-product ansatz modelled on Derrida–Evans–Hakim–Pasquier's ASEP solution, giving exact spin currents and NESS phase diagrams.

reason: ETH reproduces the FDT; it is not the same law. It is a mechanism (Srednicki 1999) and holds up to finite-size corrections.

fix.summary: In the ETH ansatz the smooth function f_O(E,ω) fixes both the spectral function and the symmetrized correlator of O. Their ratio is the equilibrium FDT at the eigenstate's temperature, so single energy eigenstates satisfy the FDT up to finite-size corrections (Srednicki 1999).

reason: This applies the FDT; it is not the same law. There is a sign error in the map, and the sideband-asymmetry interpretation has measurement-backaction subtleties.

fix.summary: A mechanical resonator's thermal force noise follows from the FDT applied to its susceptibility, and cavity sideband cooling engineers a colder effective bath. The Stokes/anti-Stokes asymmetry (∝n̄+1 vs n̄) reflects quantum FDT/zero-point fluctuations and serves as a thermometer, although detector-noise correlations complicate its interpretation.

reason: The interferometer SQL comes from the imprecision–backaction trade-off, not directly from the FDT. Mechanism, not identity.

fix.summary: The quantum FDT, with ħω coth(ħω/2k_BT) in place of 2k_BT, leaves zero-point noise at T=0. That vacuum noise, together with the imprecision–backaction trade-off, sets the standard quantum limit of linear amplifiers (Caves) and interferometers. Squeezing redistributes the noise between quadratures and cannot remove it.

reason: The map is dimensionally inconsistent: with ṗ=−αp, α is a rate and k_BT=D_p/(mα). Use friction F=−αv instead.
Populations decouple into a Pauli master equation only in the Davies weak-coupling secular limit. Coherences break the identity. The Fokker–Planck claim is loose.

fix.summary: The Lindblad equation is the general Markovian quantum master equation. In the weak-coupling secular (Davies) limit its energy-basis populations obey a classical Pauli rate equation with detailed balance at the bath temperature, and quantum-jump unravellings play the role of stochastic trajectories.
fix.breaks: Coherences between energy levels, and non-secular or non-Markovian dynamics, have no classical rate-equation counterpart.

reason: Misstated exponents. Homogeneous-gas KZ data matched 3D XY (z≈3/2, ν≈2/3). Donner et al. measured ν≈0.67 from the correlation length in equilibrium.

fix.summary: Quenching a homogeneous Bose gas through T_c freezes in coherence domains whose size scales as τ_Q^{ν/(1+zν)}. The measured KZ exponent (≈0.35) is consistent with 3D XY dynamics (ν≈0.67, z≈3/2), and equilibrium correlation-length measurements in trapped gases gave ν≈0.67.

reason: Entanglement scaling is a diagnostic used to extract c, so method transfer fits better. Specify the geometry: c/3 holds for an interval in an infinite or periodic system.

fix.summary: At a 1+1D quantum critical point the entanglement entropy of an interval in an infinite or periodic chain grows as (c/3) ln L (c/6 for an open-chain end), so the central charge labelling the universality class is read off numerically from entanglement. Gapped 1D phases obey an area law instead.

reason: Kibble–Zurek sweeps measure the combination ν/(1+zν), not ν and z separately.

fix.summary: Rydberg-blockade tweezer arrays and trapped-ion crystals implement transverse-field and long-range Ising models with hundreds of spins. Slow sweeps through their quantum critical points measure Kibble–Zurek scaling of the ordered domain size, which gives the exponent combination ν/(1+zν).

reason: A record with breaks is not an identity. The breaks are also misplaced: the LHY correction is a density effect, and the fermionic crossover mean field is only qualitative at unitarity.

fix.summary: The Gross–Pitaevskii equation is Hartree mean-field theory for a condensate, with the macroscopic wavefunction as the order parameter of a Ginzburg–Landau-type functional. For fermions, BCS mean-field theory with a self-consistent chemical potential interpolates from BCS pairs to molecular BEC across a Feshbach resonance.
fix.breaks: GP is a T=0 dynamical equation, not a free energy near T_c, and fails in strongly fluctuating 1D gases. Beyond-mean-field (Lee–Huang–Yang) terms matter at higher density, and crossover mean field is only qualitative at unitarity.

reason: Mean-field exactness comes from all-to-all coupling, a mechanism rather than an identity. With cavity loss κ the critical coupling changes from the closed-system λ_c.

fix.summary: Atoms coupled to one cavity mode interact all-to-all, so the Dicke/Hepp–Lieb superradiant transition is exact in mean field as N→∞. A BEC in a pumped cavity realized it as self-organization into a checkerboard lattice, an open-system transition with Landau order parameter ⟨a⟩ whose threshold is shifted by cavity loss κ.

reason: The third law maps only in unattainability form; the Nernst form fails for extremal holes. laws-of-thermodynamics is the better node.

fix.summary: The zeroth, first and second laws of black-hole mechanics are the laws of thermodynamics, with temperature ħκ/2πck_B and entropy A/4ℓ_P². Hawking radiation made this physical. The third law holds only in unattainability form, since extremal black holes have non-zero entropy at κ=0.

reason: This is a derivation from assumed horizon thermodynamics, not the same law in both notes. It relies on a local-equilibrium assumption, and entropic gravity is disputed.

fix.breaks: It assumes local equilibrium and S∝A for every local Rindler horizon. Higher-curvature theories need non-equilibrium entropy production (Eling–Guedens–Jacobson). Verlinde-style entropic gravity is disputed, for example by neutron-interference objections.

reason: Rényi replicas (n→1, no quenched disorder) did not descend from the spin-glass n→0 trick. They share an analytic-continuation device, so this is an analogy.

fix.summary: The Page curve was justified by a replica computation: Rényi entropies Tr ρ^n from gravitational path integrals on n-fold covers, with replica wormholes as saddles that couple replicas, continued to n→1. Spin-glass theory uses the same device for ⟨ln Z⟩, continuing n→0, where saddles that couple replicas encode disorder averaging.
fix.breaks: The limits differ (n→1 vs n→0), and black holes have no explicit quenched disorder unless the gravity dual is an ensemble (JT). Parisi replica-symmetry breaking has no established gravitational counterpart.

reason: Calling −3/2 ln A universal is contested, since other LQG countings give different log coefficients. Matching A/4 by fixing Immirzi is criticized. This is microcanonical counting applied, so method transfer.

fix.summary: In loop quantum gravity, horizon microstates are spin-network punctures carrying area quanta. Microcanonical counting gives S∝A, which matches A/4 only for a fixed Barbero–Immirzi parameter, and some countings give a −(3/2)ln A correction.
fix.breaks: The logarithmic coefficient depends on the counting scheme (−3/2 vs −1/2 in different treatments). Fixing γ by matching A/4 is criticized as a tuning, not a prediction.

reason: 'Exactly' holds only at leading order in large charges for 5D BPS black holes.

fix.summary: Strominger and Vafa counted the D-brane bound states carrying the charges of a 5D extremal BPS black hole and found S=ln Ω=A/4G at leading order in large charges. This is a microcanonical derivation of Bekenstein–Hawking entropy via the Cardy formula of the dual 2D CFT.

reason: Field-level generic overlap with no specific map. The content is covered by C1394 (Bekenstein entropy) and C1395 (Page curve).
Calling A/4ℓ_P² the largest entropy any region holds is the later, contested holographic bound (it fails for spacelike regions). Hawking fixed the coefficient 1/4.

fix.summary: Bekenstein argued from information theory that a horizon must carry entropy proportional to its area, measuring information hidden from outside observers, and that a generalized second law must hold. Hawking's temperature fixed the coefficient: S_BH=k_BA/4ℓ_P².

reason: This applies random-state typicality to evaporation, not the same law. It is not standard graduate stat-mech, so strength 2.

fix.summary: Page's result for the average entanglement entropy of a subsystem of a random pure state (nearly maximal until it is half the system) gives the Page curve. Unitary evaporation requires the radiation's fine-grained entropy to rise and then fall, unlike Hawking's monotonic thermal result.

reason: A bound and a conjecture are not an identity. The idea migrated from black-hole entropy. The naive spacelike area bound fails; Bousso's covariant bound replaces it.

fix.summary: Black-hole entropy scaling with area rather than volume led to the Bekenstein bound and the holographic principle of 't Hooft and Susskind: the degrees of freedom in a region are bounded by its boundary area in Planck units. Bousso's covariant light-sheet bound is the consistent general form, and it defeats extensive counting at gravitational scales.

reason: The emission is a Planck spectrum filtered by greybody factors. The Stefan–Boltzmann law on horizon area misstates the luminosity: effective cross sections and species counts matter (Page 1976).

fix.summary: Bogoliubov mixing of in- and out-modes at a horizon gives exactly Bose–Einstein (Fermi–Dirac for fermions) occupation numbers at T_H, filtered by greybody factors. The mass-loss rate is therefore Stefan–Boltzmann-like, L∝AT_H⁴∝M⁻², with a coefficient set by the greybody factors and the number of emitted species.

reason: A specific application, but one-sided (a GW detector applying the FDT), so not structural in stat mech. Strength 2.
Applies the Kubo formula holographically, so method transfer. The value holds for Einstein-gravity duals; higher-derivative corrections violate it as a bound.

fix.summary: The shear viscosity of a strongly coupled plasma follows from the Kubo formula (the low-frequency stress-tensor retarded correlator), computed holographically as graviton absorption by a horizon. For any Einstein-gravity dual η/s=ħ/4πk_B, far below quasiparticle kinetic-theory estimates. Higher-derivative gravity can go lower, so it is not a strict bound.

reason: For N=4 SYM on S³ this is a deconfinement-like large-N transition on a compact space, not confinement in the usual QCD sense.

fix.summary: In global AdS, thermal radiation and large black holes exchange dominance in a first-order Hawking–Page transition at T~1/ℓ_AdS. Via AdS/CFT this is a large-N deconfinement transition of the dual gauge theory on S³ (Witten), with free energy jumping from O(1) to O(N²) and the Polyakov loop as order parameter.

reason: This is a mechanism (an exponential density of states), not an identity. The Hagedorn idea came from hadrons (1965), and the phase-transition reading (Atick–Witten) is an interpretation.

fix.summary: Exponentially growing state densities, ρ(m)~e^{m/T_H} (Hagedorn 1965 for hadrons, later strings), make the canonical partition function diverge at T_H. In string theory this is usually read, following Atick–Witten, as a phase transition, an analogue of deconfinement, rather than a true limiting temperature.

reason: The fixed point is evidenced only in truncated functional RG and is unproven. That is not graduate-course structural, so strength 2, and the name overstates Wilson–Fisher.

fix.name: Asymptotic safety: a non-Gaussian RG fixed point for gravity
fix.breaks: The existence of the fixed point rests on truncations of the functional RG, and its Lorentzian meaning and unitarity are unsettled.

reason: One-sided: cosmology uses the Boltzmann equation. It is specific but not structural in stat mech, so strength 2.
The shared ingredient is causality implying analyticity; particle dispersion relations did not come from stat-mech linear response. Mechanism, not method transfer.

fix.summary: Causality makes both the photon vacuum-polarization function and linear-response susceptibilities analytic in the upper half-plane, giving Kramers–Kronig-type dispersion integrals. For muon g−2 this turns σ(e⁺e⁻→hadrons) data into the leading hadronic contribution, which is now in tension with lattice determinations.

reason: Enhancement from scale to conformal invariance is proven only in 2D (with unitarity) and is strongly supported in 3D. 'Locality' alone is not sufficient.

fix.summary: At continuous transitions, scale invariance with locality and unitarity enhances to conformal invariance: proven in 2D, strongly supported in 3D. The fixed point is then a CFT whose operator dimensions are the critical exponents and whose OPE data fix all correlations.

reason: This is the Standard-Model thermal transition studied with stat-mech tools, a shared object rather than the same law in both notes.
The bootstrap is a technique carried over, not an identity. 'Highest precision' holds for 3D Ising but not for every O(N) model.

fix.summary: Conformal bootstrap constraints (crossing symmetry plus unitarity) fix the 3D Ising exponents to the highest precision available, ν≈0.62999 and η≈0.03630, beyond Monte Carlo and the ε-expansion. For O(N) models they are competitive with Monte Carlo.

reason: This is a universality argument applied, not an identity. N_f=2 O(4) assumes a strong U_A(1) anomaly, and recent lattice work questions first order for N_f=3.

fix.summary: Symmetry and ε-expansion arguments put the two-flavour chiral transition in the 3D O(4) class if the U_A(1) anomaly stays strong, while three massless flavours were argued to give a first-order transition (cubic determinant term). Physical quark masses give a crossover at T_pc≈156 MeV with O(4)-like scaling in lattice data, and recent lattice studies question the N_f=3 first-order prediction.

reason: Same mean-field form but different physics: a T=0 Lorentz-invariant vacuum versus a thermal free energy of charge-2e pairs. That makes it an analogy, which needs a breaks.

fix.summary: The Higgs potential has the Landau–Ginzburg form with a negative quadratic term, and its vacuum is the broken-symmetry minimum. Coupling to gauge fields gives the Anderson–Higgs mechanism first seen in Ginzburg–Landau superconductors, where the photon acquires mass 1/λ_L as W and Z do.
fix.breaks: The GL coefficients are thermodynamic (a∝T−T_c) for a charge-2e pair field. The Higgs potential is a zero-temperature quantum effective potential in a Lorentz-invariant theory, and local gauge symmetry cannot break spontaneously (Elitzur).

reason: Sign error in the gap equation: with ⟨q̄q⟩<0, M=m−2G⟨q̄q⟩.
The Higgs mass term is not the only relevant operator; the cosmological constant is also relevant (the second hierarchy problem).

fix.summary: Apart from the cosmological constant, the Higgs mass term is the only relevant operator of the Standard Model. Keeping m_h≪Λ requires tuning the bare parameter near its critical value, just as a magnet must be tuned to T_c for ξ≫a. Naturalness asks what symmetry or dynamics does the tuning.

reason: Trivial: the Carnot bound applies to every heat engine and nothing here is reactor-specific. The decay-heat remark is filler.
The QCD critical point is conjectural and the caloric-curve plateau's interpretation is debated. It is a shared phase-diagram structure, not an identity. Strength 2.

fix.summary: Strongly interacting matter has a nuclear liquid–gas first-order line at μ_B≈0.92 GeV ending in a critical point (T_c≈15–18 MeV from multifragmentation data), and a conjectured chiral/deconfinement line at high μ_B whose endpoint would be in the 3D Ising class. Coexistence obeys Gibbs conditions in (T, μ_B), and the meaning of caloric-curve plateaus is debated.

reason: This is thermodynamics with two conserved charges applied, so mechanism, not identity. Gibbs versus Maxwell depends on surface tension.

fix.summary: With two conserved charges (baryon number and electric charge), a first-order hadron–quark or liquid–gas transition in a star can form a Gibbs mixed phase instead of a sharp Maxwell interface; large surface tension favours the Maxwell case. At the base of the inner crust, Coulomb frustration of phase separation produces 'pasta' phases (rods, slabs).

reason: RMT's main migrations were to quantum chaos, mesoscopic transport and localization. Calling it 'core' for spin glasses overstates it.

fix.summary: Wigner introduced random matrices to model the dense resonances of compound nuclei. Level repulsion (Wigner surmise) and Porter–Thomas width distributions, organized by Dyson's symmetry classes, became core tools for quantum chaos, mesoscopic transport and localization.

reason: A niche phenomenological model whose identification of percolation with deconfinement is disputed. Confidence should be proposed.
A proposal cannot be an identity. Name the dispute: the entropy definition and the entropy–multiplicity link are model-dependent.

fix.breaks: The proposal rests on a dipole-cascade model, and identifying the entropy with final-hadron multiplicity is assumed. H1 comparisons are suggestive, but alternative definitions of proton entanglement entropy give different results.

reason: The map mislabels the pion gas's ~3 degrees of freedom as ε/T⁴. A 20% deficit is reproduced by resummed weak coupling (HTL), so it does not show strong coupling.

fix.summary: An ideal QGP is a relativistic Bose (gluons) plus Fermi (quarks) gas, ε/T⁴=(π²/30)(16+(21/2)n_f), and the jump from ~3 pion degrees of freedom to ~47.5 signals deconfinement. Lattice pressure reaches ~80% of this at a few T_c, a deficit that resummed (HTL) perturbation theory largely reproduces.

reason: A linear branching process has no saturation term, so equating it with directed percolation is an overclaim. It is critical Galton–Watson branching, the mean-field limit.

fix.summary: Neutron chains are a branching process, and criticality k_eff=1 is the critical point of Galton–Watson branching (the mean-field limit of absorbing-state transitions, with zero population absorbing). Reactor-noise methods (Feynman-α, Rossi-α) use the fluctuations that diverge as k→1 to measure subcriticality.
fix.breaks: Neutron chains are linear, with no density-dependent saturation, so they are not directed percolation beyond mean field. Real reactors are stabilized by thermal feedback, not by fluctuations.

reason: Freeze-out gives n/p≈1/6. Free neutron decay until deuterium forms (T≈0.07 MeV) lowers it to ≈1/7, and that sets Y_p≈0.25.

fix.summary: The n/p ratio tracks its equilibrium value e^{-Q/T} until weak rates Γ∝G_F²T⁵ fall below the Hubble rate H∝T²/M_Pl at T_f≈0.8 MeV, freezing n/p≈1/6. Neutron decay until the deuterium bottleneck breaks lowers it to ≈1/7, giving Y_p≈2(n/p)/(1+n/p)≈0.25.

record.name: Many-body localization as a failure of ETH
record.summary: Strong disorder in interacting chains produces emergent local integrals of motion (l-bits), so eigenstates violate ETH: area-law entanglement, Poisson level statistics, and memory of initial conditions. Whether MBL survives in the thermodynamic limit (avalanche instability) is contested.

record.name: Landauer bound in quantum thermodynamics
record.summary: Erasing a bit costs at least k_BT ln2. In quantum thermodynamics this becomes the Reeb–Wolf equality: dissipated heat is at least T times the reduction in the system's von Neumann entropy, with finite-size corrections, and it underlies the resource theory of thermal operations.
